questions.q:
(a) Change 4500 cm³ into litres. [1]
(b) Change 0.8 m² into cm². [1]
questions.tip: Square the length conversion for area (100² = 10 000), cube it for volume.

questions.q:
A semicircle has diameter 12 cm.
(a) Find its area. Give your answer in terms of π. [1]
(b) Find its perimeter. Give your answer in terms of π. [2]
questions.model:
(a) Radius 6 cm. Area = ½ × π × 6² = 18π cm².
(b) Curved part = ½ × π × 12 = 6π. Perimeter = 6π + 12 cm.
questions.tip: The perimeter of a semicircle includes the straight diameter.

questions.q:
A sector of a circle has radius 12 cm and angle 150°.
(a) Find the area of the sector. Give your answer in terms of π. [2]
(b) The two straight edges of the sector are joined to make a hollow cone. Find the radius of the base of the cone. [2]
questions.model:
(a) Area = 150/360 × π × 144 = 60π cm².
(b) Arc length = 150/360 × 2π × 12 = 10π cm. This becomes the circumference of the base:
2πr = 10π → r = 5 cm.
questions.tip: When a sector is rolled into a cone, the arc becomes the base circumference and the radius becomes the slant height.

questions.q:
A cylinder of radius 5 cm contains water to a depth of 8 cm.
A solid metal sphere of radius 3 cm is placed in the cylinder and is completely covered by the water.
[The volume of a sphere is V = 4/3 πr³.]
(a) Calculate the rise in the water level. [3]
(b) Write down the new depth of the water. [1]
ms: (a) M1: volume of sphere 4/3 × π × 3³ (= 36π or 113.1)
questions.model:
(a) Volume of sphere = 4/3 × π × 27 = 36π cm³.
Rise h: π × 5² × h = 36π → 25h = 36 → h = 1.44 cm.
(b) 8 + 1.44 = 9.44 cm.
questions.tip: The water rises by the volume of the sphere divided by the cross-sectional area of the cylinder.

questions.q:
A solid is made from a hemisphere of radius 6 cm with a cone of radius 6 cm on top. The total height of the solid is 14 cm.
[Volume of sphere = 4/3 πr³, surface area of sphere = 4πr², volume of cone = 1/3 πr²h, curved surface area of cone = πrl.]
(a) Show that the volume of the solid is 240π cm³. [3]
(b) Calculate the total surface area of the solid. [3]
questions.model:
(a) Hemisphere height = radius = 6 cm, so cone height = 14 − 6 = 8 cm.
Hemisphere: ½ × 4/3 × π × 216 = 144π.
Cone: 1/3 × π × 36 × 8 = 96π.
Total = 240π cm³.
(b) Slant height l = √(6² + 8²) = 10 cm.
Curved hemisphere = ½ × 4π × 36 = 72π. Cone = π × 6 × 10 = 60π.
Total = 132π = 414.69… ≈ 415 cm² (no flat faces, as the circles are joined together).
questions.tip: Do not include the circular base of the hemisphere or the cone: those faces are glued together inside the solid.

questions.q:
AB is a chord of a circle, centre O, radius 9 cm. AB = 12 cm.
(a) Show that angle AOB = 83.6°, correct to 1 decimal place. [2]
(b) Calculate the area of the minor segment cut off by AB. [4]
(c) Calculate the perimeter of the minor segment. [2]
ms: (a) M1: sin(½ AOB) = 6/9 or cosine rule cos AOB = (81 + 81 − 144)/(2 × 9 × 9)
(b) M1: triangle area ½ × 9 × 9 × sin 83.6 (= 40.2 or 40.3)
questions.model:
(a) The perpendicular from O bisects AB, so sin(½ AOB) = 6 ÷ 9.
½ AOB = 41.81°, so AOB = 83.62… = 83.6°.
(b) Sector = 83.62/360 × π × 81 = 59.11 cm².
Triangle = ½ × 9 × 9 × sin 83.62° = 40.25 cm².
Segment = 59.11 − 40.25 = 18.86 ≈ 18.9 cm².
(c) Arc = 83.62/360 × 2π × 9 = 13.14 cm. Perimeter = 13.14 + 12 = 25.1 cm.
questions.tip: Keep the unrounded angle in your calculator for later parts; rounding early can change the third figure.
